From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up & MAP draft: technical eval plan (post-demo recap)

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — really appreciated your time. Per our call, I put together a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the technical evaluation milestone we agreed on. The draft is attached (ACME_MAP_Draft_v2.xlsx) and includes suggested milestones, owners, target dates, and dependencies.

Key items from our call:
- Goal: Validate model quality and production economics for ACME's customer support summarization pipeline by EOD Nov 5.
- Primary success criteria: P95 generation latency <= 200ms on 8-token responses for our target throughput profile; average cost per 1M tokens <= $X (TBD after quantization profile); ROUGE / semantic similarity to baseline >= 0.88 for extractive summaries (we'll refine metric).
- Shortlist: redwood-compat gpt-like open models (Llama 2 13B q4, Mistral/Redwood-verified medium), and a 4-bit quantized variant for latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Evaluation plan: benchmark harness + 1k representative prompts, throughput test at 200 requests/min, and latency percentile reporting (P50/P90/P95/P99).
- Data & security: ACME will share a sanitized prompt set and a small sample dataset (no PII).

Requested next steps:
1) Review MAP draft and confirm owners & target dates (I suggested owners in the sheet).
2) ACME to share sanitized prompt set by Oct 8.
3) Redwood to deliver benchmark spec and test harness by Oct 12 (we'll attach benchmark-specs.pdf).
4) Run initial bench and sync on Oct 20 for results & next actions.

Marissa, adding you as the internal owner for running the benchmark once we get the prompt set. Alex/Priya — let me know if any of these targets look off.

Thanks,
Camila
--

- We'll test the following model variants: Llama 2 13B q4f16, Mistral 7B v2 (fp16), and a Redwood-verified 13B quantized variant (q4) to measure latency/cost tradeoffs.
